title: Liberal Education course
description: A general education course outside the major, chosen from the university's liberal education lists in areas such as the arts and humanities, history, social sciences, literature, and the biological sciences, or on themes such as civic life and ethics.
notes: UMN liberal education cores and themes.

title: Liberal Education course or WRIT 1301
description: In one of these two first-year semesters the student takes a first-year writing course on academic reading, argument, research, and revision; in the other, a general education course from the university's liberal education lists.
notes: UMN lists 'Liberal Education course or Writ 1301' in both first-year semesters (all_in_any_order group). Official WRIT 1301 description is in data/raw/umn/courses/.

title: Additional Science Requirement
description: A second natural science course chosen from a short approved list, such as further physics, general chemistry, earth science, or a biology or psychology course with a science focus.
notes: UMN: Chem 1071/65, Phys 1302W, ESci 2201, Psy 3011, or GCD 3022 (3-4 credits).

title: UD Math Oriented Requirement
description: An upper-level mathematics-oriented course chosen from an approved list, such as further linear algebra, probability, numerical analysis, combinatorics, or logic.
notes: UMN: counts toward the 23 credits of technical electives plus math-oriented requirement.

title: Technical Elective
description: An upper-level computer science course chosen by the student from an approved list. Common options cover areas such as machine learning, security, graphics, networking, databases, and software engineering.
notes: UMN: technical electives plus the math-oriented requirement total at least 23 credits, at least 11 of them CSci.

title: Open Elective
description: Any course the student chooses, inside or outside the major, that counts toward the degree. Students often use free electives for a minor, extra courses in the major, or personal interests.
notes: UMN: taken if needed to reach 120 credits.
